---
title: "EPM occupancy (manuscript)"
sample_data:
    - filename: DLC_single-mouse_EPM.predictions.h5
      with_video: true
---

A two-panel figure on an elevated plus maze (EPM) dataset: a napari-style
snapshot of a single video frame overlaid with keypoints and short trailing
tracks (**A**), alongside the occupancy heatmap of the mouse's centroid
across the whole session (**B**).

## Imports and style

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from movement import sample_data
from movement.filtering import (
    filter_by_confidence, rolling_filter, interpolate_over_time
)
from movement.plots import plot_occupancy

from movement_figures import (
    apply_style,
    figure_size,
    move_colorbar_to_divider,
    napari_canvas_screenshot,
    reserve_colorbar_space,
    save_figure,
)

apply_style("manuscript")
```

## Load and prepare data

We fetch the EPM sample dataset together with its still frame,
then apply a two-step cleaning pipeline:
a confidence filter followed by a rolling median filter.

```{python}
ds = sample_data.fetch_dataset(
    "DLC_single-mouse_EPM.predictions.h5", with_video=True
)
frame = plt.imread(ds.frame_path)
frame_h, frame_w = frame.shape[:2]

position_conf = filter_by_confidence(
    ds.position, ds.confidence, threshold=0.95
)
position_clean = rolling_filter(
    position_conf, window=5, statistic="median", min_periods=2
)
ds["position"] = position_clean
```

We also grab a napari canvas screenshot of a single frame, with the tracked
points and a short (10-frame) trailing track, mirroring what the
[`movement` GUI](https://movement.neuroinformatics.dev/latest/user_guide/gui.html)
would show: the video loaded via the `napari-video` plugin, and the dataset's
points/tracks layers as added by the `movement` napari plugin.

```{python}
FRAME_SEC = 285  # time (s) of the snapshot; mouse is in an open arm here
TAIL_SEC = 2     # number of seconds to show in the trailing track tail
frame_index = int(FRAME_SEC * ds.fps)
tail_length = int(TAIL_SEC * ds.fps)

napari_frame = napari_canvas_screenshot(
    ds, ds.video_path,
    frame_index,
    tail_length=tail_length,
    zoom=True,
    display_text=True,
)
```

## Build the figure

```{python}
fig, (ax_napari, ax_heat) = plt.subplots(
    1, 2, figsize=figure_size("double", height=4.0)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Panel A: napari canvas screenshot                                   #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
ax_napari.imshow(napari_frame)
ax_napari.set_title("Video frame with tracked keypoints")
ax_napari.axis("off")
reserve_colorbar_space(ax_napari)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Panel B: occupancy heatmap                                          #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
ax_heat.imshow(frame, cmap="gray")

# Bins of 30x30 pixels, covering the whole frame.
BIN_PIX = 30
bins = [
    np.arange(0, frame_w + BIN_PIX, BIN_PIX),
    np.arange(0, frame_h + BIN_PIX, BIN_PIX),
]

_, ax_heat, _ = plot_occupancy(
    da=position_clean,
    ax=ax_heat,
    bins=bins,
    alpha=0.8,
    cmin=10,  # hide bins with fewer than 10 frames
    norm="log",
)
move_colorbar_to_divider(ax_heat, "# frames")
ax_heat.set_xlim(0, frame_w)
ax_heat.set_ylim(frame_h, 0)
ax_heat.set_title("Occupancy heatmap")
ax_heat.axis("off")
```

## Save the figure

```{python}
fig_name = "epm_occupancy"
save_paths = save_figure(fig, fig_name, formats=("pdf", "svg"))
print(f"Saved '{fig_name}' figure to {save_paths[0].parent}.")
```
